candidates.function: Plant one owned food unit from a living plant in a small hand-dug plot, where it may root as a new plant under the existing plant rules; inspect units, sites, plants and plot progress; cancel unfinished planting.
candidates.costs: Study: 3 rounds. Plant: inputStackId names one whole owned, untreated, unspoiled food unit (quantity 1; one plot per unit) gathered from a living plant; stock still on a plant is not owned. x, y: a 0.25 m plot within reach on ordinary meadow soil (.), waterlogging at most 0.1, soil moisture 0.3-1.2, 0.6 m clear of objects and people, fewer than 3 plants of that food within 5 m. Three paid rounds of 1 energy: loosen, place, cover; plant resumes paused work after rechecking reach, site, unit and energy. Inspect and inspect-progress: one round, 0.2 energy. Inspect: inputStackId checks a unit (with x, y also a site for it), or target a plant source or plot in reach. Inspect-progress: target a plot in reach. Maintain: refused at no cost. Cancel: one round, no energy. Harvest uses gather. No tool, water or seed is given.
candidates.effects: Loosening keeps the unit carried, owned and ageing. Placing moves it, with origin and age, into the open plot, where it cannot be eaten or used. Covering completes planting, not establishment: the plot becomes a propagule exactly like a naturally dispersed one, rooting only through actual temperature, light, soil moisture and season; cold, darkness or drought stall it; if the buried unit spoils first, the plot dies. On rooting, the unit becomes a new plant with no stock (ceiling 4), regrowing under the natural rule, harvested by anyone with gather; a ledger records growth and units produced and removed. Nothing is copied or guaranteed. A unit check reports decay, treatment, origin and whether it can be planted, never viability. Inspect-progress reports visible changes since your last look, else inconclusive; trial window 120 rounds, checks every 10; not a growth date. Maintain: no water transfer, amendment or hand-changeable obstruction exists. Records are unverified. An unworked round pauses; low energy, leaving reach or a changed site pause without charge; a lost or spoiled unit stops the work. Cancel, or death, before placing returns the unit once (where the person died); after placing, the unit stays uncovered, does not root and ages. No reward or refund.
Actual nutrition and toxicity apply. Food never directly heals. resource:ID selects an owned stack.

response.text: {"queries":[],"result_json":"{\"reviews\":[{\"actor\":\"moss\",\"decision\":\"develop\",\"ability\":null,\"reason\":\"Develop a minimal unheated preparation operation, not cooking. Related-capability searches returned gathering, eating and planting, while the full probe contract supports only observation or a small material trial. None performs meal-scale preparation. Prior root consumption supports considering an unheated meal, but does not establish the present roots' cleanliness or safety. Seven owned roots are available; no vessel, water, tool, heat source or suitable fuel is established. A dry, whole-root preparation is a feasible limited function for the current-conversation development handoff. No waiting for implementation advances the world.\",\"specification\":\"Implement the general operation 'Prepare unheated food', parameterized by mode (inspect, prepare, inspect-progress, cancel), owned input stack ID, and positive whole-unit quantity. It applies to food that can actually be handled and prepared without cutting, water or heat; it is not specific to moss or roots. The minimal prepare mechanism is manual removal of loose surface debris followed by separation of selected whole units into an inspectable food lot. It neither peels nor sterilizes, cooks, invents ingredients, or makes unsuitable food edible. Reuse open.probe@foundation-open@1 observation logic where applicable, and the existing owned-stack, reservation, decay and transfer code; record these dependencies and reused code in the implementation, rather than presenting them as new inventions. New work is the paid preparation process and conserved food-lot output. Do not invoke probe's destructive physical-trial mode as a substitute for this process.\\nInputs and references: resolve exact owned item IDs, not nearby plant stock or resource-name matches. For moss, item-3-moss-30 is the available root stack, quantity 7 and recorded decay 50.27044688; revalidate current quantity, ownership, reach, condition and accessibility at execution. The earlier planting inspection is incomplete and older, not a current safety certificate. Knowledge record root reports nutrition 14 and toxicity 0 observed at tick 48; retain its evidence scope rather than declaring every root safe. item-23-moss-260, quantity 0.9 branch, is not an ingredient or assumed fuel and remains untouched. Other applicants may use their own applicable food stacks. No hidden resources or facts are disclosed.\\nPrerequisites: independently completed study, usable hands, sufficient energy, physical reach to the input, and an actually supportable unheated preparation method for that food. No ground contact is required: work on one held whole unit at a time. If holding or preparation would require an unavailable implement or support, fail that prerequisite explicitly. Ordinary soil is not a clean preparation surface. Surface observations report only detectable spoilage, dirt and physical changes; lack of visible defects is not proof against unobservable hazards. Obvious spoiled or unsuitable units are not marked ready. Unknown safety remains explicitly unknown.\\nCosts and progress: study takes 2 rounds independently for each learner. Inspection costs 1 active round and 0.2 energy and consumes no food. Preparation costs 1 active round and 0.5 energy per whole unit, including its visible condition check and manual brushing. A quantity of seven therefore requires seven completed work rounds and 3.5 energy, in addition to any separately requested inspection, study, travel or transfer. Validate before each charge. Each completed unit produces one distinct processed unit or a stack-compatible addition to the prepared lot; unusable units remain identified, unprepared inputs. Emit a truthful unsuitable-unit result for a paid check that cannot prepare its unit. Never debit an entire batch in advance. No water, branch, fuel or edible material is consumed by this minimal whole-unit method. Only actual removable loose debris may be displaced; do not create collectible material stock from cosmetic debris. If debris removal would remove edible matter or require unsupported treatment, stop that unit rather than silently reducing mass.\\nConservation and products: selected food units move from input to an owned prepared-food lot with unchanged edible quantity, origin, age, existing treatment history and decay trajectory. Record the actual dry-brushing treatment, original stack reference and per-unit outcome. Preserve represented nutrition, toxicity and spoilage effects; preparation cannot refresh food, improve nutrition or override hazards. Prepared and remaining units together equal the original food units, less only consumption or other independently logged actions. The lot consists of real roots, not a new free meal token or duplicated inventory. It can be inspected, transferred and eaten through the existing food interfaces. Do not assert successful cleanliness if the physical operation did not remove the observed loose debris.\\nLifecycle: reserve only the pending unit against conflicting use. Track job ID, actor, resolved input IDs, requested quantity, completed-unit IDs, charges, current stage and failure reason. Leaving reach, insufficient energy, loss of usable hands or an invalid input pauses remaining work without further charge. Resume rechecks prerequisites and current food condition without resetting decay or repeating completed charges. Cancellation releases any surviving unprocessed reservation exactly once; completed lots remain actual products. Death ends work, releases remaining reservations through the existing death/inventory rules and leaves completed products subject to those rules. Do not conjure a return to a dead actor's inventory. No refund of elapsed time, spent energy or completed physical work. An interrupted atomic unit step commits neither its charge nor its output; committed steps cannot be refunded or repeated as free output. Global development/review pauses preserve work without advancing time.\\nOngoing effects and sharing: no passive preparation, automatic maintenance, heating or continuing fuel process exists. Food keeps ageing under its existing rules, including while paused; dry preparation grants no shelf-life extension. Subsequent rechecking or re-preparation requires another real paid action. Sharing is optional and separate. Reuse give (forest.give, foundation-forest@1; 1 round, 0.5 energy, whole owned units and actual adjacent recipient), and eat (forest.eat, foundation-forest@1; 1 round, 1 energy and actual consumed units), with their exact schemas and validation. Actual participants must independently communicate willingness, accept applicable transfers and choose whether to eat. Preparation cannot issue their actions, infer consent, feed neighbors or alter their inventory without an executed authorized transfer. Implement all established checks and transitions in code; do not require repeated model approval.\",\"learning\":2,\"experienceReview\":\"No experience, pleasure or satisfaction is awarded for this review, study, a request, naming a lot or starting work. Preparation itself supplies no automatic mood or nutrition bonus. Actual meals use the existing consumption rules and actual nutrition; mood must not reduce basic nutrition. Actual observation may provide evidence-backed information gain, including a genuinely informative preparation failure, but inspection requests and repeated unchanged results do not qualify. Do not add a new preparation reward channel or duplicate rewards already attributed to observation, eating or social participation. Any existing event-based pleasure or maintained-satisfaction mechanism must retain its personal-applicability tests, bounded amount and cap, decay, cooldown and functional deduplication; ordinary familiar meal participation need not be novel. If those mechanisms lack executable eligibility and bounds, this capability awards zero rather than inventing them. No physical-comfort award is specified; the global comfort cap remains 10. Protected reward accounts, budgets, goals and permissions remain unchanged.\",\"visualReview\":\"Emit observable start, paid unit-check, debris-removal, unit-completion, pause, resume, cancel and failure events only when their respective actions occur. Use reusable metadata keyed by job ID and input/output item IDs: operation, stage, completed/requested units, visible condition, treatment, raw/unheated status, safety-unknown status where applicable, event time and failure reason. Preserve the roots' existing appearance while allowing an evidence-based reduction of visible loose dirt; no cooked color, steam, fire, vessel or cleanliness/safety seal is generated. Partial progress shows only completed units and the pending count, never a completed batch. Unsupported or failed preparation displays its actual failure and unchanged or genuinely changed material, not a successful meal. Shared-meal visuals require real independently executed transfers, consumption or communication events, not nearby neighbors or the applicant's intention.\"}]}"}
